subject: sst
prompt_en: Name three mahajanapadas and their capitals.
prompt_hi: 3 mahajanapada aur unki rajdhaniyon ke naam batao.
answer: For example: Magadha – Rajagriha (later Pataliputra); Kosala – Shravasti; Vatsa – Kaushambi; Avanti – Ujjayini; Vajji – Vaishali; Gandhara – Takshashila (Taxila); Kashi – Varanasi.

subject: sst
prompt_en: On a map, Magadha sits on the Ganga plains in south Bihar, with rivers around it and hills around Rajagriha. Describe in words two map features that helped Magadha grow strong.
prompt_hi: Map par Magadha dakshin Bihar ke Ganga maidan mein hai, aas-paas nadiyaan hain aur Rajagriha ke chaaron taraf pahadiyaan. Shabdon mein do aisi map wali cheezein batao jinse Magadha shaktishaali bana.
answer: Rivers (like the Ganga and Son) gave water for farming, transport for trade and natural protection; the fertile plains grew plenty of food; the hills around Rajagriha acted as a natural defence wall.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare a mahajanapada ruled by a raja with a gana-sangha like the Vajjis: who decided, and how?
prompt_hi: Raja wale mahajanapada aur Vajji jaise gana-sangha ki tulna karo: faisla kaun leta tha, aur kaise?
answer: In a kingdom, one raja (often from one family) made the main decisions, collected taxes and led the army. In a gana-sangha, a group of leaders met in an assembly, discussed and decided together.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Think of how decisions are made in your school or housing society. Is it more like a raja or a gana-sangha? Explain.
prompt_hi: Socho aapke school ya society mein faisle kaise hote hain. Kya woh zyada raja jaisa hai ya gana-sangha jaisa? Samjhao.
answer: A good answer identifies who decides (e.g. a principal alone, or an elected committee that meets and votes) and correctly labels it as more like a raja (one person decides) or a gana-sangha (a group decides together in a meeting).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why did the spread of iron tools help cities to grow?
prompt_hi: Lohe ke auzaaron ke failne se shehar badhne mein madad kyun mili?
answer: Iron axes and ploughs helped clear forests and farm more land, so farmers grew more food than they needed (a surplus); this extra food could feed people in towns — craftspeople, traders, soldiers and officials.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if farmers had grown only just enough food for their own families, what would have happened to cities, crafts and armies?
prompt_hi: Socho: agar kisaan sirf apne parivaar jitna hi anaaj ugaate, toh shehron, kaarigaron aur senaon ka kya hota?
answer: Cities, crafts and armies could not have grown, because there would be no extra food to feed people who did not farm, and no surplus for rulers to tax.

subject: sst
prompt_en: An archaeologist finds a small, bent piece of silver stamped with symbols like a sun and a wheel, but no king's name. What is it probably, and what does it tell us?
prompt_hi: Ek archaeologist ko chaandi ka ek chhota, muda hua tukda milta hai jis par suraj aur pahiye jaise nishaan thape hain, par kisi raja ka naam nahi. Yeh shayad kya hai, aur isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer: Probably a punch-marked coin, among the earliest coins in India; it tells us that people were buying and selling with money, so trade was growing in this period.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend how a small janapada could become a powerful mahajanapada with a city capital. Use Magadha as your example.
prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki ek chhota janapada kaise ek shaktishaali mahajanapada ban sakta tha jiski rajdhani ek shehar ho. Magadha ka example lo.
answer: Key idea: a jana settles (janapada); with iron tools and fertile land it grows a surplus; rulers collect taxes, build forts and armies, conquer neighbours and become a mahajanapada; trade and crafts make the fortified capital (Rajagriha, later Pataliputra) a city.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why did rajas build strong walls around their capitals and collect taxes?
prompt_hi: Raja apni rajdhaniyon ke chaaron taraf mazboot deewarein kyun banwaate the aur kar (tax) kyun lete the?
answer: Walls protected the city, its people and its wealth from attacks by rival kingdoms; taxes paid for the army, the walls, officials and the king's court.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Pataliputra was built where the Ganga and Son rivers meet. Why was this a smart place for a capital?
prompt_hi: Pataliputra wahan bana jahan Ganga aur Son nadiyaan milti hain. Rajdhani ke liye yeh samajhdaari ki jagah kyun thi?
answer: The rivers gave water for farming, easy boat transport for trade and moving armies, and acted as natural moats that made the city harder to attack.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Order these from earliest to latest: Kalinga war; Chandragupta Maurya founds the empire; Bindusara becomes king; Alexander reaches north-west India (326 BCE).
prompt_hi: Inhe sabse pehle se baad ke kram mein lagao: Kalinga yuddh; Chandragupta Maurya samrajya banate hain; Bindusara raja bante hain; Sikandar uttar-pashchim India pahunchta hai (326 BCE).
answer: Alexander reaches the north-west (326 BCE) → Chandragupta founds the empire (c. 321 BCE) → Bindusara becomes king (c. 297 BCE) → Kalinga war (c. 261 BCE).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Who helped Chandragupta Maurya come to power, and which famous text is linked to him?
prompt_hi: Chandragupta Maurya ko satta tak pahunchne mein kisne madad ki, aur unse kaunsa prasiddh granth juda hai?
answer: Chanakya (also called Kautilya); the Arthashastra, a text on running a state.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name three ways the Mauryas kept control over such a huge empire.
prompt_hi: 3 tareeke batao jinse Mauryon ne itne bade samrajya par niyantran rakha.
answer: Dividing it into provinces run by princes or governors; appointing officials and tax collectors; keeping a large army; using spies to report what was happening; building roads to connect regions.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Ashoka's edicts have been found from Kandahar in Afghanistan to Karnataka in the south, and from Gujarat to Odisha. Describe in words what this spread of find-spots on a map tells us.
prompt_hi: Ashoka ke shilalekh Afghanistan ke Kandahar se dakshin mein Karnataka tak, aur Gujarat se Odisha tak mile hain. Shabdon mein batao ki map par yeh failaav humein kya batata hai.
answer: The empire (or at least Ashoka's reach and messages) stretched across most of the subcontinent — from the north-west to the south and from west to east; only the far south lay outside it.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why did Ashoka change his way of ruling after the Kalinga war?
prompt_hi: Kalinga yuddh ke baad Ashoka ne raaj karne ka tareeka kyun badla?
answer: He saw the huge suffering — deaths, injuries and people taken from their homes — and, as he wrote himself, felt deep regret; he gave up wars of conquest and chose to rule through dhamma.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare how Chandragupta built his empire with how Ashoka ruled after Kalinga.
prompt_hi: Chandragupta ne samrajya kaise banaya aur Kalinga ke baad Ashoka ne kaise raaj kiya — tulna karo.
answer: Chandragupta built it by conquest, a strong army and careful statecraft (advised by Chanakya). After Kalinga, Ashoka kept the empire but stopped wars of conquest, ruled through dhamma, sent officials to spread its message, and cared for people's welfare (wells, rest houses, care for animals).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistakes: "Ashoka's edicts were written in English on paper and posted to every village."
prompt_hi: Galti dhoondho: "Ashoka ke shilalekh angrezi mein kaagaz par likh kar har gaon mein bheje gaye."
answer: They were carved on rocks and stone pillars (not paper), mostly in Prakrit using the Brahmi script (some in the north-west in Greek, Aramaic and Kharosthi) — English did not exist then.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Where in your daily life do you see a symbol from Ashoka's time? And what one message would you carve on a "dhamma pillar" at your school today?
prompt_hi: Roz ki zindagi mein Ashoka ke zamaane ka koi nishaan tum kahan dekhte ho? Aur aaj apne school ke "dhamma stambh" par tum kaunsa ek sandesh likhoge?
answer: The lion capital (national emblem) on currency notes, coins, passports and government documents; the Ashoka Chakra on the national flag. A good message echoes dhamma — kindness, respect for everyone, non-violence, care for animals and nature.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if Ashoka's messages had been written on wood or cloth instead of stone, what would we know about him today?
prompt_hi: Socho: agar Ashoka ke sandesh patthar ki jagah lakdi ya kapde par likhe hote, toh aaj hum unke baare mein kya jaante?
answer: Very little from his own words — wood and cloth rot away; much of our knowledge of Ashoka comes from stone edicts that survived for over 2,000 years (and were read again after James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in the 1830s).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a younger cousin how Magadha became the Mauryan empire and how Ashoka ruled it. Use at least four steps.
prompt_hi: Chhote cousin ko samjhao ki Magadha kaise Maurya samrajya bana aur Ashoka ne ise kaise chalaya. Kam se kam chaar steps mein.
answer: Key idea: Magadha's resources made it strong; Chandragupta with Chanakya founded the Mauryan empire (c. 321 BCE); it was run through provinces, officials, army and spies; Ashoka fought the Kalinga war, regretted it, and ruled through dhamma, spreading it with edicts.

subject: sst
prompt_en: An edict says everyone in Ashoka's empire was happy and well cared for. How should a historian treat this claim?
prompt_hi: Ek shilalekh kehta hai ki Ashoka ke samrajya mein sab khush the aur sabka dhyaan rakha jaata tha. Itihaaskar ko is daave ko kaise dekhna chahiye?
answer: As the ruler's own view and goals — useful evidence of what Ashoka wanted and believed — but it must be checked against other sources (archaeology, other texts, foreign accounts) before accepting it as what really happened.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Using a map of this period, describe in words where each ruled: the Satavahanas, the Kushanas, the Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas, and Kharavela.
prompt_hi: Is samay ke map ko dekh ke shabdon mein batao ki kaun kahan raaj karta tha: Satavahana, Kushana, Chola-Chera-Pandya, aur Kharavela.
answer: Satavahanas: the Deccan (today's Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra region). Kushanas: the north-west and north, from Central Asia and Afghanistan into the Ganga plains (Mathura). Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas: the far south (Tamil Nadu and Kerala). Kharavela: Kalinga (today's Odisha).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare one big empire (like the Mauryas) with many regional kingdoms (like the period after them): one advantage and one challenge of each.
prompt_hi: Ek bada samrajya (Maurya jaisa) aur kai kshetriya rajya (unke baad jaise) compare karo: har ek ka ek fayda aur ek mushkil.
answer: Big empire: one set of rules and roads over a huge area (advantage) but hard to control far regions (challenge). Regional kingdoms: rulers close to local people, local languages and art grew (advantage) but more rivalry and wars between kingdoms (challenge).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why did Roman traders want to trade with south India?
prompt_hi: Roman vyapaari dakshin Bharat se vyapar kyun karna chahte the?
answer: South India had goods Romans prized — especially black pepper, along with other spices, fine cotton cloth, pearls and gems — and Romans paid in gold and silver coins, wine and other goods.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Sailors learned to use the seasonal monsoon winds to cross the Arabian Sea directly. Predict what sea trade would have been like without these winds.
prompt_hi: Naavikon ne seekha ki mausami monsoon hawaon ka use karke Arabian Sea seedha paar kiya ja sakta hai. Socho: in hawaon ke bina samudri vyapar kaisa hota?
answer: Slower, riskier and costlier: ships would have to hug the coast, take longer routes and make fewer trips, so less trade would reach India and Rome.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why was the Satavahana king called "Gautamiputra" Satakarni? What does this tell us?
prompt_hi: Satavahana raja ko "Gautamiputra" Satakarni kyun kaha jaata tha? Isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer: "Gautamiputra" means "son of Gautami" — Satavahana kings were often known by their mother's name, which shows that mothers held an important place in how royal identity was shown.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A Kushana gold coin shows a king in Central Asian dress on one side and the Buddha on the other. List three things a historian can learn from it.
prompt_hi: Ek Kushana sone ke sikke par ek taraf Madhya Asiya ke kapdon mein raja hai aur doosri taraf Buddha. Itihaaskar ise dekh ke 3 kya baatein jaan sakta hai?
answer: Who the ruler was and how he wanted to be seen; that the Kushanas had Central Asian roots; that they respected or supported Buddhism; that the kingdom was rich and traded widely (it could mint gold coins).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistake: "Roman coins found in south India prove that the Romans ruled south India."
prompt_hi: Galti pakdo: "Dakshin Bharat mein mile Roman sikke saabit karte hain ki Romans ne dakshin Bharat par raaj kiya."
answer: Finding foreign coins shows trade, not rule: Roman traders paid with them for Indian goods. There is no evidence that Rome ruled south India.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare Buddha images in the Gandhara style and the Mathura style.
prompt_hi: Gandhara shaili aur Mathura shaili ki Buddha moortiyon ki tulna karo.
answer: Gandhara (north-west): influenced by Greek and Roman art — wavy hair, heavy folded robes, realistic face, often grey stone. Mathura: local style — reddish sandstone, rounder fuller figure, smiling face, thin clinging robe. Both show the Buddha but in different local styles.

subject: sst
prompt_en: What are the Sangam texts, and what do they tell us?
prompt_hi: Sangam granth kya hain, aur ve humein kya batate hain?
answer: Early Tamil poems composed over several centuries around this time; they describe life in the far south — kings (Cheras, Cholas, Pandyas), landscapes, love, war, trade and ports.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Think of something in your home that came from far away. How does it reach your town today, compared with how pepper reached Rome 2,000 years ago? What travels along with goods besides the goods themselves?
prompt_hi: Ghar mein koi cheez socho jo door se aayi ho. Aaj woh tumhare shehar tak kaise pahunchti hai, aur 2,000 saal pehle kaali mirch Rome tak kaise pahunchti thi? Saamaan ke saath aur kya-kya safar karta hai?
answer: Today: trucks, trains, container ships, planes, online orders; then: carts, pack animals, sailing ships using monsoon winds. Along with goods travel people, languages, ideas, food habits, art and religions.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend why historians call this period an "age of reorganisation" and not an age of decline. Give three pieces of evidence.
prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki itihaaskar is daur ko "punargathan ka yug" kyun kehte hain, patan ka nahi. 3 saboot do.
answer: Key idea: power was reorganised among many regional kingdoms, each with achievements. Evidence: growth of trade with Rome and Central Asia (Roman coins, ports); new coins (Indo-Greek portraits, Kushana gold, Satavahana coins); art and literature (Gandhara and Mathura art, Sangam poems); spread of Buddhism along trade routes.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why did Buddhism spread to Central Asia and China during this period?
prompt_hi: Is samay Buddh dharm Madhya Asiya aur China tak kyun faila?
answer: Monks travelled with merchants along the busy trade routes, and rulers like the Kushana king Kanishka supported Buddhism; monasteries along the routes became resting places for traders and teachers.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Put these Gupta rulers in order: Chandragupta II, Samudragupta, Kumaragupta, Chandragupta I.
prompt_hi: In Gupta rajaon ko sahi kram mein lagao: Chandragupta II, Samudragupta, Kumaragupta, Chandragupta I.
answer: Chandragupta I → Samudragupta → Chandragupta II → Kumaragupta.

subject: sst
prompt_en: The Prayag pillar inscription, written by the court poet Harishena, praises Samudragupta's victories. What can it tell us, and what should we be careful about?
prompt_hi: Prayag stambh lekh, jo darbaari kavi Harishena ne likha, Samudragupta ki jeeton ki tareef karta hai. Isse kya pata chalta hai, aur kis baat ka dhyaan rakhna chahiye?
answer: It tells us which rulers and regions Samudragupta fought or made submit, and how he wanted to be remembered. But it is a prashasti (praise poem) by his own court poet, so it is one-sided and may exaggerate; we check it against coins and other sources.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name Aryabhata's famous book and two of his ideas.
prompt_hi: Aryabhata ki prasiddh kitaab ka naam aur unke do vichaar batao.
answer: The Aryabhatiya (499 CE). Ideas: the Earth spins on its axis (causing day and night); eclipses are caused by shadows; a very accurate value of pi (about 3.1416); use of the place-value system.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Aryabhata said the stars only seem to move across the night sky. What did he say was really happening?
prompt_hi: Aryabhata ne kaha ki taare raat ke aasmaan mein sirf chalte hue lagte hain. Unke hisaab se asal mein kya ho raha tha?
answer: The Earth itself spins on its axis, so the sky appears to move — like trees seeming to run backwards when you sit in a moving train.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistake: "A lunar eclipse happens because the moon is switched off for a while, and Aryabhata agreed with this."
prompt_hi: Galti dhoondho: "Chandra grahan isliye hota hai kyunki chaand kuch der ke liye band ho jaata hai, aur Aryabhata bhi yahi maante the."
answer: Wrong: a lunar eclipse happens when the Earth comes between the sun and the moon and its shadow falls on the moon; Aryabhata explained eclipses using shadows.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why do scientists still study the iron pillar at Mehrauli in Delhi?
prompt_hi: Vaigyanik aaj bhi Delhi ke Mehrauli ke loh stambh ka adhyayan kyun karte hain?
answer: Although it is made of iron and has stood in the open for about 1,600 years, it has hardly rusted; it shows the advanced metal-working skill of the time, and scientists study how its special composition and protective layer resist rust.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name the great Sanskrit poet-playwright of this period and two of his works.
prompt_hi: Is kaal ke mahaan Sanskrit kavi-naatakkaar ka naam aur unki do rachnaayein batao.
answer: Kalidasa; Abhijnanashakuntalam and Meghaduta (also Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava).
